# Investment Memorandum

## 1. Executive Summary

- In March 2025, Honda Canada Finance Inc. and its banking syndicate executed a first amendment to extend the Tranche A Commitment Termination Date by one year.
- Honda Canada Finance Inc., a Canadian corporation, serves as the Borrower under a third amended and restated credit agreement originally dated March 25, 2024, with Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce as Administrative Agent.
- The banking syndicate includes major Canadian and international banks: Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce, Bank of Montreal, Royal Bank of Canada, The Toronto-Dominion Bank, MUFG Bank Ltd. (Canada Branch), Mizuho Bank Ltd. (Canada Branch), The Bank of Nova Scotia, National Bank of Canada, and Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation (Canada Branch).
- The primary purpose of this amendment is to extend the Tranche A Commitment Termination Date from March 25, 2025 to March 25, 2026, providing Honda Canada Finance with continued access to credit facilities for an additional year.
- Honda Canada Finance Inc. is the Canadian financing subsidiary of Honda Motor Company, providing automotive financing services in the Canadian market.

## 2. Investment Highlights & Risks

### Key Strengths / Credit Positives:
• Strong sponsor backing from Honda Motor Company, a globally recognized automotive manufacturer with established market presence
• Diversified banking syndicate comprising major Canadian banks (Big Six banks) and established Japanese financial institutions, indicating broad lender confidence
• Long-standing credit relationship with multiple amendments dating back to 2014, demonstrating sustained banking relationships
• Borrower representations confirm no material adverse changes, no defaults, and compliance with existing covenants

### Principal Risks and Mitigating Factors:
• Limited financial information available in the amendment document restricts comprehensive credit assessment
• Automotive finance sector exposure to economic cycles and interest rate fluctuations
• Extension request may indicate potential refinancing needs or market conditions affecting longer-term financing availability
